title: UniPoolerV2._dispatch (verbatim copy) has no non-default-hook guard: an index-4 cutover that skips or reorders setHook leaves the no-op DefaultDispatchHook wired, so every index-4 mint succeeds while accruing zero phUSD mint-debt
borderlineNote: Medium is arguable on the M-04 precedent (same class filed Medium). Kept Low because the debt is protocol-own revenue, recoverable by an owner mint, and no party profits. If the owner considers mintDebt load-bearing for phUSD backing/emission accounting, re-weigh to Medium.
description: CODE-001 (cross-contract chain: three owner writes on three contracts plus replaceDispatcher(4); only the setHook omission fails open). LOCAL-UP-001 adds the BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook-has-no-hookTypeId detail. FAITH-003 is the story-side annotation and is folded in, not filed separately.
impact: Protocol-own revenue accounting: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.mintDebt (ratio% of dispatched USDS, realised by pull() as phUSD minted to the protocol's own recipient) silently stays 0 for every index-4 mint while the DefaultDispatchHook is wired. No user funds move; no third party gains; USDS still flows into POL. The shortfall is reconstructible from Dispatched/mint events and can be made good by an owner mint. Secondary facet: separate-tx setDispatcher/replaceDispatcher ordering opens a fail-LOUD index-4 mint outage window (OnlyDispatcher revert), no loss.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys UniPoolerV2 (ctor wires no-op DefaultDispatchHook)
2. Cutover replaceDispatcher(4) executes before / without setHook(BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook)
3. Every index-4 mint succeeds; _dispatch has no non-default-hook guard; onDispatch is a no-op
4. mintDebt never accrues; no revert, no event signalling the omission
likelihood: low-medium - requires an owner sequencing omission in a multi-step, multi-contract cutover; non-obvious because NudgeRatchet (M-04 fix) fails closed in the identical situation
assumptions: Non-malicious owner; setHook skipped or reordered in the story-048 cutover
severityJustification: Non-obvious Law-3 footgun, so in scope, but impact is a recoverable, attacker-less under-accrual of the protocol's own mint-debt (no theft, no user loss, no availability loss). Severity follows the closest sibling L-09 (Uniboost, same base-class fail-open, open Low) rather than M-04: M-04's Medium predates the established sibling precedent and the M-04 fix is per-concrete. Q-08's wont-fix rationale (live, no retrofit) does not transfer to undeployed UniPoolerV2 - a pre-deploy guard is cheap.
recommendation: Concrete-only guard on UniPoolerV2 (store default hook, require(address(hook) != defaultHook)) or add hookTypeId() to the pooler hook. Cutover: setHook before or atomically with replaceDispatcher(4); hook.setDispatcher last or same tx.
safeConfigGuidance: Add a concrete-only guard (stored defaultHook compared in _dispatch, or hookTypeId() on the pooler hook) pre-deploy, with a story-048 verbatim-clause waiver; otherwise setHook before or atomically with replaceDispatcher(4), and verify a DebtAccrued on the first index-4 mint.
knownIssueCheck: No KI match. KI#4 (owner trust for registering dispatchers) does not cover it: forgetting/reordering setHook on an index-4 cutover is a NON-OBVIOUS Law-3 footgun (precedent: M-04 c91bef813d was filed Medium on the same class). In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority.
ledgerMatch: None by fingerprint. Same CLASS as Q-08 96c60b723f (wont-fix, BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch), L-09 563df2e64a (open, Uniboost), M-04 c91bef813d (fixed).
secondaryFacet: Fail-LOUD mint outage window: with hook.setDispatcher (plan step 6) and replaceDispatcher (step 8) in separate Ledger txs, index-4 mints through the still-registered BalancerPoolerV2 revert OnlyDispatcher in between; batchMint too if BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.dispatcherIndex == 4. No funds lost. Same mitigation (atomic ordering), so kept inside this finding.
law2Annotation: story-048 mandates a verbatim _dispatch. FAITH-003: the code is faithful; the story is NOT unsafe (owner-omission footgun, not an exploit). A concrete-only guard (constructor-supplied hook, or stored defaultHook compared in _dispatch) is Law-1-sanctioned; if the owner adopts the in-_dispatch guard, record a waiver on the verbatim clause so later Law-2 scans do not flag it.

priorWontFixDisclosure.label: Q-08
priorWontFixDisclosure.triageReasonVerbatim: Owner REJECTED — intentional: BalancerPoolerV2 is LIVE and will not be retrofitted with the hookTypeId guard. The guard asymmetry vs NudgeRatchet is an accepted operational state on a deployed contract (Law-3 owner-trusted). Valid finding, accepted-not-fixed (not a false-positive — the guard genuinely is absent; the owner accepts the exposure on the live contract).
priorWontFixDisclosure.whyNotTransferred: Q-08's rationale is scoped to BalancerPoolerV2 being LIVE and not retrofittable. UniPoolerV2 is a new, UNDEPLOYED contract (story-048 gates its deployment on this audit); adding a guard is a pre-deploy choice, not a retrofit. Different contract, different fingerprint: a new instance, not a reopen of Q-08. Q-08 itself stays wont-fix and is NOT attached to.
